newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares fall on dashed hopes of "package".
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares fall on dashed hopes of "package".

text.p: Delhi shares closed sharply lower on Monday as the government's failure to announce a package of measures to shore up capital markets by the end of January prompted heavy sales, brokers said.
The Delhi sensitive index closed 18.59 points, or 2.54 percent, lower at 713.06.

"It seems that the market is heading for another bearish phase as major players feel that the governemnt might mot announce any measures to boost the capital market in view of the annual budget ahead," said S.C. Juneja of brokers Jaico Credit.
The budget for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) is expected to be presented by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on February 28.

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda left on Friday on a week-long trip to attend the annual World Economic Forum summit at Davos. Contrary to market expectations, he did not announce any new steps to bolster the capital markets before leaving.
Chidambaram said on Thursday that decisions already taken last month by the government to spur the economy amounted to a package of economic reforms.
State Bank of India shed 16.45 rupees at 258.55.
Larsen and Toubro was down 4.0 rupees at 232.
